summary:
DEMO DATA: Contoso CloudWatch is a fictional company and every ticket in this report is synthetic. This section is where you write your executive summary: 4-6 bullets, strengths first, then the biggest levers.

  • Lead with what works, e.g. first response and first contact resolution.
  • Explain the big numbers, e.g. how much open time is spent waiting on customers.
  • Name the systemic drivers: product, self-service and process, not people.

All teams: Example: account access and licensing make up most Customer Care volume. Both are candidates for self-service.
Example: errors after upgrades show up across several themes. Publishing known issues at release time would head off repeat tickets.
Customer Care: Example: password reset and invitation-link failures are the top driver and are resolved quickly, but they're avoidable.
Technical Support: Example: most open time is spent waiting for customers to send logs or test a fix. Tickets close only after several follow-up reminders.

improve.title: 1. Keep noise out of the queue
improve.body: Auto-replies, bounces and spam reach agents.
bullets: Rules to auto-close auto-replies and bounces.
Move test tickets to a sandbox group.

improve.title: 2. Self-service account access
improve.body: Account access is the top commercial driver.
bullets: Show a specific error when a reset link fails.

improve.title: 3. Knowledge base for repeat how-to questions
bullets: Guides for thresholds, custom checks and maintenance windows.

agentLead: Recognition of the practices behind the team's strongest results. Agents are compared only within their own team.

agents.title: Example: what great looks like
bullets: Explain the root cause, not just the fix.
Follow up proactively and set expectations for next steps.
Acknowledge the business impact before troubleshooting.

method:
Demo data: generated by demo/Generate-DemoData.ps1. In a real run, every ticket's conversation is read by AI agents against prompts/tagging-instructions.md, and the metrics are calculated from Freshdesk timestamps.

Definitions: first response is measured in weekday hours; FCR is the share of resolved tickets closed with two or fewer customer replies; 'closed after customer stopped responding' is detected from the follow-up note patterns in config.json; 'time waiting on customer' splits open time by who spoke last.
